rules.title: Weak or ambiguous wording
rules.message: "{match}" is imprecise — use "shall" for an obligation, or state the measurable property

rules.title: Negation
rules.message: "{match}" is a negative — state what the system shall do, not what it shall not do

rules.title: Superfluous infinitive
rules.pattern: \b(have the ability to|be capable of|be designed to|be able to|be used to)\b
rules.message: "{match}" is unnecessary — state the requirement directly with "shall"

rules.title: Escape clause
rules.pattern: \b(as far as (?:is )?possible|as little as possible|as much as possible|where possible|if possible|if necessary|if required|if needed|as needed|to the extent (?:necessary|practical|practicable)|as appropriate|as required|if it should prove necessary|if practicable|wherever practical|to the greatest extent)\b
rules.message: "{match}" lets the supplier decide whether to comply — state the condition explicitly or drop it

rules.title: Oblique requirement
rules.message: "{match}" is oblique — use "and" or "or", not both; spell out alternatives separated by "and" or "or"

rules.title: Purpose clause
rules.pattern: \b(with the intent of|in order to|so as to|so that)\b
rules.message: "{match}" states why — state what behaviour shall be satisfied instead

rules.title: Passive voice
rules.message: Possible passive voice "{match}" — use active voice (e.g. "The system shall…")

rules.title: Vague quantifier
rules.pattern: \b(some|several|many|few|minimal|maximal|enough|sufficient|a lot of|a number of|a few|a couple of)\b
rules.message: Vague quantifier "{match}" — use a specific number or value

rules.title: Pronoun
rules.message: Pronoun "{match}" — name the specific entity (e.g. "the system" rather than "it")

rules.title: Absolute term
rules.message: Absolute term "{match}" — qualify with conditions or tolerances (e.g. "under normal load" rather than "always")

rules.title: Combinator
rules.message: Combinator "{match}" — split into separate, independently verifiable requirements

rules.title: Temporal indefinite
rules.pattern: \b(in a timely manner|in due course|when convenient|as soon as|eventually|promptly|at last)\b
rules.message: Temporal indefinite "{match}" — specify a concrete deadline or interval (e.g. "within 500 ms")

rules.title: Open-ended clause
rules.pattern: (\b(including but not limited to|such as|and so on|and so forth|among others)\b|\betc\.?)
rules.message: "{match}" leaves the set undefined — enumerate every item that must be satisfied

rules.title: Placeholder
rules.message: Placeholder "{match}" — replace with concrete content before review

rules.title: Abbreviation
rules.message: Abbreviation "{match}" — spell out in full (e.g. "for example" rather than "e.g.")

rules.title: Non-atomic requirement
rules.message: Multiple conjunctions around "{match}" — consider splitting into separate requirements

rules.title: Parentheses
rules.message: Parenthetical "{match}" — integrate the content into the main sentence or create a separate requirement

rules.title: No obligation verb
rules.message: No obligation verb found — add "shall", "must", "will", or "is required to"{match}
